leads.question: Rerun stage B of cycles/017/hyperevm.work/v3check_rest.py over the same 7,000 groups with the sampling seed recorded and every mismatch saved in full, then run chkmis.py on each. Does any swap still fail to reproduce once the 0xd78218c0 Mint variant and the two missing factories are applied, and if so which mulDiv or getAmount call in the step differs from src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 and src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol?
leads.why: These 7 are the only unexplained outputs of a closed producer on the 512 bit branch of FullMath. A residual that is not a collector gap would be validator arithmetic that differs from the source, which any account could use against v4 pools on HyperEVM.

leads.question: Does go1.26.10 contain the 1.26 backport (#81865, CL 841425) of Go issue 81863, and if it does not, does any function of bor v2.11.1, bsc v1.8.2 and libevm/coreth under avalanchego 1.15.3 core/vm, core/state or holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 and v1.2.4 store through a pointer chosen between two stack locals, the shape cycle 10 searched for in Nitro 0e44603? leads.why: Every validator of these networks may be built by the same toolchain, so a miscompiled handler would make the whole chain compute a result that differs from the specification while every endpoint agrees with every other.

leads.question: Grep holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 and v1.2.4, core/vm and core/state of bor v2.11.1, bsc v1.8.2, avalanchego 1.15.3, celo op-geth c7ed55b8 and Nitro's fork for every int8, int16 or int32 conversion that is then compared with a constant wider than its type (the Go issue 82839 shape). For each hit, build the function with the installed go toolchain at the affected and the fixed form of the issue's reproducer and say whether the branch can be wrongly taken, and which opcode or copy offset it serves.
leads.why: theme-library-paths located no such comparison but did not search the source systematically. A hit on SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, a shift or a memory offset path would change TickMath, TickBitmap or BalanceDelta results on every node built with go1.26.6 to go1.26.10.

leads.question: From category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp at v0.16.5 (the copy in cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5, lines about 1380 to 1540), prove or refute that the block-exit writer gives the same final stack for every iteration order of dep_counts: does the spill step before line 1415 remove every dependency cycle, is a dependency skipped at the avx_reg check ever read from a register that an earlier write in the loop reassigned (yx1 is rebound to the AVX register of each element processed), and can an element whose stack offset lies below min_delta be left with a nonzero count?
leads.why: v0.16.5 validators run different machine code for the PoolManager depending on heap layout. Only four layouts were tested. A clobbering order would make some validators compute different PoolManager state from the same block.

leads.question: For the set 1 and set 2 scripts that never finish on Polygon, Monad and Tempo, which endpoint of each network accepts a gas cap large enough (or serves debug_traceCall with a higher cap), and do they match the stored Ethereum hash when run to completion? For the worst such swap, what gas does it use on each of the three networks against that network's per-transaction gas limit?
leads.why: These swaps cross the most ticks and are the only pool-math scripts never compared on these networks. A swap that cannot fit in a transaction on a network that prices storage higher is also an A9 hazard for the pools that reach that state.

leads.question: Transfer of the HyperEVM L-185 check: trace every MegaETH and Monad PoolManager transaction (51,233 on MegaETH per cycle 15) for one that ends with an ERC-20 still synced (CURRENCY_SLOT nonzero at its end) and see whether a later transaction in the same block settles native value or an ERC-20 without its own sync.
leads.why: MegaETH's sequencer is closed and parallel, and Monad executes optimistically in parallel. The transaction boundary of transient storage on their producers rests on validator replay and source reading. A leaked sync lets a later settle be credited with a balance rise someone else paid (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364).
